1	# Generic-coverage routine
2	
3	Weekly Claude routine (on a strong model), offline on a fresh clone. Goal: make the **generic**
4	generic extractor — `extension/event-extractors/generic-extractor.js` and the
5	shared `extension/event-extractors/helpers/*.js` — recover **more** of what the
6	dedicated per-site sources get, measured by the generic-coverage gate. **Most runs
7	correctly change nothing** — the gate already banks every prior win, so a new
8	generic win is rare and a forced or fake one is worse than none. No win → no branch,
9	no PR.
10	
11	## 1. Scope — the strong model runs only because the cheap gate already passed
12	
13	This task is a two-tier run, cheap gate first: the **scheduler** (a pure-code Action,
14	no model at all) ran this task's precondition (`task.mjs`, over the `commits` signal),
15	and only *because* it found a meaningful change did it dispatch you — a strong-model
16	subagent — via the `ready-for-agent` issue. Most weeks the gate skips and no strong
17	model ever boots; you are paid for solely on the weeks there's real work. (This is
18	the "cheap dispatcher front door" cost model — the scheduler precondition is that
19	front door, cheaper than a dispatcher session because it runs no model.)
20	
21	So **you don't re-run that gate.** The dispatch issue's **Context** names the
22	substantive commits in the window; treat it as binding scope and don't re-litigate
23	whether to run. Still: **most runs correctly change nothing** (below), so "ran" never
24	means "must produce a PR".
25	
26	## 2. Measure the baseline
27	
28	```sh
29	npm install && npm run test:live
30	```
31	
32	The gate prints a "bare generic value differences (informational)" block and a
33	per-exemplar matrix (✓ match · ~ different value · ✗ missing · — n/a): a `~` is a
34	concrete generic gap the extractor gets wrong, a `✗` a field it finds nothing for —
35	your candidate targets. This run is your pre-change reference (the committed
36	`generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json`); don't `git stash`/rerun to re-derive
37	it — that conflicts on the `ours`-driver GENERATED artifacts. A committed baseline
38	listing **fewer** `cases` than the live run is pre-existing drift, not something
39	your change introduced. Gate mechanics: [the gcec pack’s RULES.md](../../RULES.md)
40	(and the gate's own headers).
41	
42	## 3. Improve — the feedback loop
43	
44	Pick one or a few `~`/`✗` gaps and close them, iterating: **hypothesize → edit only
45	the generic extractor / helpers → `npm run test:live` → compare to the baseline**,
46	until you have one or more clean wins (or conclude there are none). Every change
47	must clear the bars **postconditions.sh** enforces in step 4 — hold to them as you
48	work, because a run that trips one there is marked **failed**:
49	
50	- **Generic only** (postcondition: *scope*). Key off a widely-used convention that
51	  would help unseen sites — display conventions (date↔time separators, start–end
52	  ranges, "Event @ Venue" titles, ordinals) or machine-readable signals (schema.org
53	  JSON-LD, OG/meta, microdata, `<time datetime>`). Lifting one `custom/<site>.js`'s
54	  logic or special-casing a host is out of scope: if the only beneficiary is a
55	  single case and the rule wouldn't fire elsewhere, it isn't generic. **The only
56	  files you may leave changed are `generic-extractor.js`, `helpers/*.js`, your
57	  covering test in `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, and the
58	  regenerated generic-coverage GENERATED artifacts** — anything else fails scope.
59	- **A real, non-regressing win** (postcondition: *win*, via the suite's gate). Every
60	  gated % must end **≥** its baseline and at least one strictly higher; a change
61	  that lifts one field but drops another isn't clean — drop it.

# Generic-coverage routine

Weekly Claude routine (on a strong model), offline on a fresh clone. Goal: make the **generic**
generic extractor — `extension/event-extractors/generic-extractor.js` and the
shared `extension/event-extractors/helpers/*.js` — recover **more** of what the
dedicated per-site sources get, measured by the generic-coverage gate. **Most runs
correctly change nothing** — the gate already banks every prior win, so a new
generic win is rare and a forced or fake one is worse than none. No win → no branch,
no PR.

## 1. Scope — the strong model runs only because the cheap gate already passed

This task is a two-tier run, cheap gate first: the **scheduler** (a pure-code Action,
no model at all) ran this task's precondition (`task.mjs`, over the `commits` signal),
and only *because* it found a meaningful change did it dispatch you — a strong-model
subagent — via the `ready-for-agent` issue. Most weeks the gate skips and no strong
model ever boots; you are paid for solely on the weeks there's real work. (This is
the "cheap dispatcher front door" cost model — the scheduler precondition is that
front door, cheaper than a dispatcher session because it runs no model.)

So **you don't re-run that gate.** The dispatch issue's **Context** names the
substantive commits in the window; treat it as binding scope and don't re-litigate
whether to run. Still: **most runs correctly change nothing** (below), so "ran" never
means "must produce a PR".

## 2. Measure the baseline

```sh
npm install && npm run test:live
```

The gate prints a "bare generic value differences (informational)" block and a
per-exemplar matrix (✓ match · ~ different value · ✗ missing · — n/a): a `~` is a
concrete generic gap the extractor gets wrong, a `✗` a field it finds nothing for —
your candidate targets. This run is your pre-change reference (the committed
`generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json`); don't `git stash`/rerun to re-derive
it — that conflicts on the `ours`-driver GENERATED artifacts. A committed baseline
listing **fewer** `cases` than the live run is pre-existing drift, not something
your change introduced. Gate mechanics: [the gcec pack’s RULES.md](../../RULES.md)
(and the gate's own headers).

## 3. Improve — the feedback loop

Pick one or a few `~`/`✗` gaps and close them, iterating: **hypothesize → edit only
the generic extractor / helpers → `npm run test:live` → compare to the baseline**,
until you have one or more clean wins (or conclude there are none). Every change
must clear the bars **postconditions.sh** enforces in step 4 — hold to them as you
work, because a run that trips one there is marked **failed**:

- **Generic only** (postcondition: *scope*). Key off a widely-used convention that
  would help unseen sites — display conventions (date↔time separators, start–end
  ranges, "Event @ Venue" titles, ordinals) or machine-readable signals (schema.org
  JSON-LD, OG/meta, microdata, `<time datetime>`). Lifting one `custom/<site>.js`'s
  logic or special-casing a host is out of scope: if the only beneficiary is a
  single case and the rule wouldn't fire elsewhere, it isn't generic. **The only
  files you may leave changed are `generic-extractor.js`, `helpers/*.js`, your
  covering test in `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, and the
  regenerated generic-coverage GENERATED artifacts** — anything else fails scope.
- **A real, non-regressing win** (postcondition: *win*, via the suite's gate). Every
  gated % must end **≥** its baseline and at least one strictly higher; a change
  that lifts one field but drops another isn't clean — drop it.
- **No illusory win** (postcondition: *jsdom*). The offline body-text scan reads
  `document.body.textContent`, which includes `<script>` JSON (Next.js
  `__NEXT_DATA__`), `<noscript>`, `<style>`, `<select>/<option>`, and CSS-hidden
  text — none of which Chrome's `innerText` exposes. A win matching only such
  content is illusory; a real one comes from visible text or a Chrome-read attribute
  (meta / JSON-LD / microdata / `<time datetime>`). **In step 4 you must pass every
  value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan** so this is checked.
  (Widening a scan-window cap can make a *different* case match a `<script>` blob it
  never reached — re-run the whole corpus before raising any cap.)
- **No forbidden win.** Don't invent `ctz` or `eventLengthInMinutes` (a wrong `ctz`
  is worse than none). `ctz` may only be *derived*, never guessed: two independent
  page-declared hints must agree — the contract
  `extension/event-extractors/helpers/derive-timezone.js` implements (#674/#676) —
  so never weaken its refusal rules for a coverage win. When a change fills a field
  generically, also check the cases whose dedicated source deliberately leaves that
  field EMPTY (stubhub/seetickets set no `ctz`) still come out empty — a "win"
  there silently breaks strict parity. `start`/`end` already match when they
  resolve to the same instant, so don't chase representation-only differences;
  never override a miss a unit test deliberately asserts.
- **Covered and clean.** Add or extend a case in
  `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, red-before-green; the full
  `npm test` must be green (postcondition: *suite*). Never weaken a test, lower the
  gate, or hand-edit a GENERATED file — commit the regenerated baseline + scorecard
  as produced.

If no clean generic win emerges, print `No generic generic-coverage improvement found.`
and stop.

## 4. Postcondition

Pass every value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan as arguments:

```sh
bash .claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/generic-extractor-improvements/postconditions.sh "<recovered value>" ...
```

- Exit 0 → the win is valid; go to step 5.
- **Non-zero → the run has FAILED.** Do not retry and do not open a PR; surface the
  failure so guiding prose can be re-introduced to this routine.

## 5. Open the PR (never merge)

Branch `claude/generic-coverage/<date>`, commit the change plus the regenerated
GENERATED artifacts, and push. Then open a **PR for review** — it never merges
itself; from there it goes through the usual flow (the gcec pack's
[merge-and-ci skill](../../skills/merge-and-ci/SKILL.md)). PR body: the
hypothesis, why it's generic (which unseen sites
it helps), how the jsdom trap was ruled out, the before→after numbers, and the
covering test.

Then log the run as a dated comment (**not** a sub-issue) on the standing
*Auto-Improvements Tracker - Generic Extractor Coverage* issue (find it **by
title**, currently #366; open it if missing, reopen it if closed) so it builds a
scrollable history, and `Refs` that issue in the PR.

1	# Generic-coverage routine
2	
3	Weekly Claude routine (on a strong model), offline on a fresh clone. Goal: make the **generic**
4	generic extractor — `extension/event-extractors/generic-extractor.js` and the
5	shared `extension/event-extractors/helpers/*.js` — recover **more** of what the
6	dedicated per-site sources get, measured by the generic-coverage gate. **Most runs
7	correctly change nothing** — the gate already banks every prior win, so a new
8	generic win is rare and a forced or fake one is worse than none. No win → no branch,
9	no PR.
10	
11	## 1. Scope — the strong model runs only because the cheap gate already passed
12	
13	This task is a two-tier run, cheap gate first: the **scheduler** (a pure-code Action,
14	no model at all) ran this task's precondition (`task.mjs`, over the `commits` signal),
15	and only *because* it found a meaningful change did it dispatch you — a strong-model
16	subagent — via the `ready-for-agent` issue. Most weeks the gate skips and no strong
17	model ever boots; you are paid for solely on the weeks there's real work. (This is
18	the "cheap dispatcher front door" cost model — the scheduler precondition is that
19	front door, cheaper than a dispatcher session because it runs no model.)
20	
21	So **you don't re-run that gate.** The dispatch issue's **Context** names the
22	substantive commits in the window; treat it as binding scope and don't re-litigate
23	whether to run. Still: **most runs correctly change nothing** (below), so "ran" never
24	means "must produce a PR".
25	
26	## 2. Measure the baseline
27	
28	```sh
29	npm install && npm run test:live
30	```
31	
32	The gate prints a "bare generic value differences (informational)" block and a
33	per-exemplar matrix (✓ match · ~ different value · ✗ missing · — n/a): a `~` is a
34	concrete generic gap the extractor gets wrong, a `✗` a field it finds nothing for —
35	your candidate targets. This run is your pre-change reference (the committed
36	`generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json`); don't `git stash`/rerun to re-derive
37	it — that conflicts on the `ours`-driver GENERATED artifacts. A committed baseline
38	listing **fewer** `cases` than the live run is pre-existing drift, not something
39	your change introduced. Gate mechanics: [the gcec pack’s RULES.md](../../RULES.md)
40	(and the gate's own headers).
41	
42	## 3. Improve — the feedback loop
43	
44	Pick one or a few `~`/`✗` gaps and close them, iterating: **hypothesize → edit only
45	the generic extractor / helpers → `npm run test:live` → compare to the baseline**,
46	until you have one or more clean wins (or conclude there are none). Every change
47	must clear the bars **postconditions.sh** enforces in step 4 — hold to them as you
48	work, because a run that trips one there is marked **failed**:
49	
50	- **Generic only** (postcondition: *scope*). Key off a widely-used convention that
51	  would help unseen sites — display conventions (date↔time separators, start–end
52	  ranges, "Event @ Venue" titles, ordinals) or machine-readable signals (schema.org
53	  JSON-LD, OG/meta, microdata, `<time datetime>`). Lifting one `custom/<site>.js`'s
54	  logic or special-casing a host is out of scope: if the only beneficiary is a
55	  single case and the rule wouldn't fire elsewhere, it isn't generic. **The only
56	  files you may leave changed are `generic-extractor.js`, `helpers/*.js`, your
57	  covering test in `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, and the
58	  regenerated generic-coverage GENERATED artifacts** — anything else fails scope.
59	- **A real, non-regressing win** (postcondition: *win*, via the suite's gate). Every
60	  gated % must end **≥** its baseline and at least one strictly higher; a change
61	  that lifts one field but drops another isn't clean — drop it.
62	- **No illusory win** (postcondition: *jsdom*). The offline body-text scan reads
63	  `document.body.textContent`, which includes `<script>` JSON (Next.js
64	  `__NEXT_DATA__`), `<noscript>`, `<style>`, `<select>/<option>`, and CSS-hidden
65	  text — none of which Chrome's `innerText` exposes. A win matching only such
66	  content is illusory; a real one comes from visible text or a Chrome-read attribute
67	  (meta / JSON-LD / microdata / `<time datetime>`). **In step 4 you must pass every
68	  value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan** so this is checked.
69	  (Widening a scan-window cap can make a *different* case match a `<script>` blob it
70	  never reached — re-run the whole corpus before raising any cap.)
71	- **No forbidden win.** Don't invent `ctz` or `eventLengthInMinutes` (a wrong `ctz`
72	  is worse than none). `ctz` may only be *derived*, never guessed: two independent
73	  page-declared hints must agree — the contract
74	  `extension/event-extractors/helpers/derive-timezone.js` implements (#674/#676) —
75	  so never weaken its refusal rules for a coverage win. When a change fills a field
76	  generically, also check the cases whose dedicated source deliberately leaves that
77	  field EMPTY (stubhub/seetickets set no `ctz`) still come out empty — a "win"
78	  there silently breaks strict parity. `start`/`end` already match when they
79	  resolve to the same instant, so don't chase representation-only differences;
80	  never override a miss a unit test deliberately asserts.
81	- **Covered and clean.** Add or extend a case in
82	  `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, red-before-green; the full
83	  `npm test` must be green (postcondition: *suite*). Never weaken a test, lower the
84	  gate, or hand-edit a GENERATED file — commit the regenerated baseline + scorecard
85	  as produced.
86	
87	If no clean generic win emerges, print `No generic generic-coverage improvement found.`
88	and stop.
89	
90	## 4. Postcondition
91	
92	Pass every value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan as arguments:
93	
94	```sh
95	bash .claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/generic-extractor-improvements/postconditions.sh "<recovered value>" ...
96	```
97	
98	- Exit 0 → the win is valid; go to step 5.
99	- **Non-zero → the run has FAILED.** Do not retry and do not open a PR; surface the
100	  failure so guiding prose can be re-introduced to this routine.
101	
102	## 5. Open the PR (never merge)
103	
104	Branch `claude/generic-coverage/<date>`, commit the change plus the regenerated
105	GENERATED artifacts, and push. Then open a **PR for review** — it never merges
106	itself; from there it goes through the usual flow (the gcec pack's
107	[merge-and-ci skill](../../skills/merge-and-ci/SKILL.md)). PR body: the
108	hypothesis, why it's generic (which unseen sites
109	it helps), how the jsdom trap was ruled out, the before→after numbers, and the
110	covering test.
111	
112	Then log the run as a dated comment (**not** a sub-issue) on the standing
113	*Auto-Improvements Tracker - Generic Extractor Coverage* issue (find it **by
114	title**, currently #366; open it if missing, reopen it if closed) so it builds a
115	scrollable history, and `Refs` that issue in the PR.

Qualify the query (`in:title "Claudinite tracker: 26 "`, or `list_issues` + `labels`) **and** pass a small `perPage` (5–10) — 27 the answer wanted is one issue or one run, never a page of them. 28 - **This repo's one divergence from the canon merge recipe: CI must be green 29 first** — twice for e2e/heavy-browser changes. Bot-blocking from CI/sandbox IPs is the 145 portable rule maintained in the canon; here the escape hatch is the 146 `SCRAPER_API_KEY` **GitHub Actions secret**, named in both tasks' 147 `required_secrets` — never a local fetch (this sandbox is bot-blocked), and 148 never an agent session. ScraperAPI is the whole fetching surface — swap the 149 vendor in that one module if it underperforms. The aid for a flaky SPA render is 150 the **`Wait-for selector`** a source request can carry 151 (`extension/events-popup/derive-wait-selector.js`, a source-request tool, NOT an 152 event extractor, #603), passed through as `wait_for_selector`. 153 - **Facebook can't be a cached live case** — a hard HTTP 400 even through the 154 proxy, so its extraction stays unit-tests-only 155 (`extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`). 156 - **Rendered output isn't deterministic.** A re-record can legitimately shift a 157 live case's `expected` — treat such drift like a site-markup change, and prefer 158 extracting JSON-LD/`og:` (which apps still inject) over brittle DOM positions. 159 - **An ambiguous numeric slash date is read by the page's declared locale, 160 centrally — never per-source, never guessed.** `"05/07/2026"` (both parts ≤ 12) 161 reads month-first by default (V8's US convention) and flips day-first only on a 162 *positive* non-US signal — an explicit non-US region in `` / 163 `og:locale`, or a non-English language; a bare `en` (region unknown) stays 164 month-first rather than guess. Resolution lives in `helpers/dates.js` 165 (`parseDateFromText` / `normalizeDateValue` take a `dayFirst` flag, threaded 166 from `generic-extractor.js`'s `pageUsesDayFirstDates`), mirroring 167 `derive-timezone.js`'s locale read; unambiguous dates (a part > 12) and the 168 `.` / `-` separators are always day-first regardless (#686). 169 - **An unrecordable page is a dead end, not a failed run.** When a fetch can't 170 produce a page (bot wall, dead URL, empty render), create-extractor's 171 preprocessing labels the request `needs-human` with the reason 172 and exits **0** — a task failure would converge to a `needs-human` dispatch 173 issue as well, duplicating the signal and implying the pipeline broke when it 174 correctly declined. Same for the pending-page sweep: the pages that did record still land. 175 - **The generic-coverage gate is a high-watermark over a changing case set.** A 176 removed/renamed case the watermark still lists makes it stale: the local refresh re-anchors it 177 (commit that); in CI it's an error to fix. *Caveat:* never commit a re-anchored 178 baseline while the gate is red — a regression bundled with a case-set change can 179 be re-anchored over. Detailed mechanics self-document in the gate's own headers 180 (`dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.js` / `.test.js`). 181 - **To see what the core generic extractor gets ON ITS OWN** on any cached page — 182 even a supported host — load the files, set `GCal.sources = []`, then call 183 `GCal.extract()`: the documented way to strip every per-site override and see 184 the bare base through the same norm/sort the popup uses. (`GCal.extract()` 185 alone no longer answers this: the generic extractor is the base layer of every 186 extraction now, so on a supported host its output already carries the site's 187 overrides.) Most start/end *differences* vs a dedicated source are just its 188 hardcoded `ctz` localizing to floating time (same instant), not extraction 189 bugs; the real gaps are fields it can't know generically (durations, 190 site-specific descriptions, and — where the page doesn't declare corroborating 191 hints, see `helpers/derive-timezone.js` — `ctz`). This is the comparison the 192 generic-coverage gate automates — and a case where it shows NO gap is a 193 candidate for deleting the per-site source and listing the host in 194 `supportedDomains`). 195 196 ## Architecture rules of the road 197 198 Whenever we agree on a new or changed top-level architectural guideline, update 199 this section as part of the same change (the design doc itself is 200 `dev/procedures/highLevelDesign.md`): 201 202 - **`extension/event-extractors/custom/` is the extensibility point — one file 203 per site, and nothing else.** The rest of `event-extractors/` is the pipeline 204 itself: the registry, the orchestrator, the shared helpers, and the one core 205 generic extractor (`generic-extractor.js`), which is a different kind of thing 206 from a per-site file. 207 - **The core generic extractor is the base layer of every extraction** — it runs 208 on every page, and a per-site source is only a layer of *overrides* merged over 209 it, stating the fields it gets better. A source never re-reads what the page 210 already says about itself, and the generic extractor may never know about a 211 specific site. 212 - **Being supported is DECLARED, never derived from the extractors.** 213 `supportedDomains` in `extension/host-lists.json` is the one list of hosts 214 we claim, read directly by the toolbar worker and the popup. Never add a second 215 list, and never register a placeholder source just to make a host count as 216 supported. The only guarded direction is that every per-site source's host 217 appears in the list. 218 - **A site we fully support gets no extractor file when there is nothing to 219 override.** It stays listed in `supportedDomains` and stays fully supported — 220 green icon, no correction prompt — with no file at all. When a 221 `custom/.js` shrinks to nothing, just delete it; when such a site starts 222 needing a fix the generic extractor can't make site-agnostically, add the file 223 back. Never keep a file whose only content is a restatement of the generic 224 base, and never annotate one as "nothing to add". 225 - Adding support for a new host is the most common change — the architecture 226 must keep it a single-file change: a host added to `supportedDomains`, plus — 227 only when the generic extractor gets that site wrong — one self-contained new 228 `extension/event-extractors/custom/.js` and a regenerated load list, 229 touching nothing else and assuming nothing about other extractors. 230 231 ## Capture policy — lessons land in the local packs 232 233 **The gcec local pack is this repo's capture surface.** Route each lesson to its 234 section here: extractor-automation to the "Extractor pipeline" section, 235 everything else to the fitting section. Mechanism before prose, per the canon's 236 local promotion ladder — `test-offline-list-sync` is this pack's worked example. 237 238 **Three kinds never land here, however strong the evidence** — filter on what a 239 lesson is *about* before picking a mechanism: 240 241 - **The owner's personal preferences** (which word means "merge it", tone, 242 summary style). They belong to the owner, are injected per-session, and change 243 without this repo hearing about it. 244 - **Claudinite loading mechanics** (which packs are declared, why a skill didn't 245 mount, why an injection missed). Engine plumbing, not project knowledge — a 246 real defect there goes upstream instead. 247 - **Anything derived from product requirements.** Packs carry 248 **development-process** lessons only; what the extension should do is 249 `dev/requirements/`'s territory, and restating it here will drift. 250 251 None of the three is mechanically checkable, so all three stay prose. 252

What the core generic extractor (`extension/event-extractors/generic-extractor.js`) recovers **on its own** for each integration-test page, compared to the full pipeline — that generic base with the page's **per-site overrides** merged over it, the reviewed-correct extraction the live test pins down. For every `dev/requirements/extractor/expected/*.json` page, `GCal.extract()` is run twice on the same cached HTML: once normally (custom) and once with the site registry emptied (the bare run), which strips every override. We grade the bare run's **primary event** (`events[0]` after the chronological sort) field-by-field against the custom primary event, counting a field only when the custom event filled it. A page where the gap closes to zero is a candidate for deleting its per-site source outright — the host stays in `supportedDomains`, so the site stays supported.

`start`/`end` count as a match when the values are byte-identical **or** resolve to the same absolute instant — a dedicated source localizing to a floating time via its `ctz` is the same moment as the bare run's offset-bearing time, not a miss (see `.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/RULES.md`). generic extractor — `extension/event-extractors/generic-extractor.js` and the
shared `extension/event-extractors/helpers/*.js` — recover **more** of what the
dedicated per-site sources get, measured by the generic-coverage gate. **Most runs
correctly change nothing** — the gate already banks every prior win, so a new
generic win is rare and a forced or fake one is worse than none. No win → no branch,
no PR.

## 1. Scope — the strong model runs only because the cheap gate already passed

This task is a two-tier run, cheap gate first: the **scheduler** (a pure-code Action,
no model at all) ran this task's precondition (`task.mjs`, over the `commits` signal),
and only *because* it found a meaningful change did it dispatch you — a strong-model
subagent — via the `ready-for-agent` issue. Most weeks the gate skips and no strong
model ever boots; you are paid for solely on the weeks there's real work.

So **you don't re-run that gate.** The dispatch issue's Context named the substantive
commits in the window (c95630e, bfbf8ca, 5427534, 3b9dfbb, 7cae2cb, d35ba2b, bce14d2,
cd99e5d, 3a33fe9, 4f66449, 84bf089, 006f686, f19eb95, e629881, 97b7df6, c52e344,
894fc67, d61e11f, 1ce76e4, 05fd5f3); treat it as binding scope and don't re-litigate
whether to run. Still: **most runs correctly change nothing** (below), so "ran" never
means "must produce a PR".

## 2. Measure the baseline

```sh
npm install && npm run test:live
```

The gate prints a "bare generic value differences (informational)" block and a
per-exemplar matrix (✓ match · ~ different value · ✗ missing · — n/a): a `~` is a
concrete generic gap the extractor gets wrong, a `✗` a field it finds nothing for —
your candidate targets. This run is your pre-change reference (the committed
`generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json`); don't `git stash`/rerun to re-derive
it — that conflicts on the `ours`-driver GENERATED artifacts. A committed baseline
listing **fewer** `cases` than the live run is pre-existing drift, not something
your change introduced. Gate mechanics: the gcec pack's RULES.md at
`.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/RULES.md` (and the gate's own headers).

## 3. Improve — the feedback loop

Pick one or a few `~`/`✗` gaps and close them, iterating: **hypothesize → edit only
the generic extractor / helpers → `npm run test:live` → compare to the baseline**,
until you have one or more clean wins (or conclude there are none). Every change
must clear the bars **postconditions.sh** enforces in step 4 — hold to them as you
work, because a run that trips one there is marked **failed**:

- **Generic only** (postcondition: *scope*). Key off a widely-used convention that
  would help unseen sites — display conventions (date↔time separators, start–end
  ranges, "Event @ Venue" titles, ordinals) or machine-readable signals (schema.org
  JSON-LD, OG/meta, microdata, `<time datetime>`). Lifting one `custom/<site>.js`'s
  logic or special-casing a host is out of scope: if the only beneficiary is a
  single case and the rule wouldn't fire elsewhere, it isn't generic. **The only
  files you may leave changed are `generic-extractor.js`, `helpers/*.js`, your
  covering test in `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, and the
  regenerated generic-coverage GENERATED artifacts** — anything else fails scope.
- **A real, non-regressing win** (postcondition: *win*, via the suite's gate). Every
  gated % must end **≥** its baseline and at least one strictly higher; a change
  that lifts one field but drops another isn't clean — drop it.
- **No illusory win** (postcondition: *jsdom*). The offline body-text scan reads
  `document.body.textContent`, which includes `<script>` JSON (Next.js
  `__NEXT_DATA__`), `<noscript>`, `<style>`, `<select>/<option>`, and CSS-hidden
  text — none of which Chrome's `innerText` exposes. A win matching only such
  content is illusory; a real one comes from visible text or a Chrome-read attribute
  (meta / JSON-LD / microdata / `<time datetime>`). **In step 4 you must pass every
  value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan** so this is checked.
  (Widening a scan-window cap can make a *different* case match a `<script>` blob it
  never reached — re-run the whole corpus before raising any cap.)
- **No forbidden win.** Don't invent `ctz` or `eventLengthInMinutes` (a wrong `ctz`
  is worse than none). `ctz` may only be *derived*, never guessed: two independent
  page-declared hints must agree — the contract
  `extension/event-extractors/helpers/derive-timezone.js` implements (#674/#676) —
  so never weaken its refusal rules for a coverage win. When a change fills a field
  generically, also check the cases whose dedicated source deliberately leaves that
  field EMPTY (stubhub/seetickets set no `ctz`) still come out empty — a "win"
  there silently breaks strict parity. `start`/`end` already match when they
  resolve to the same instant, so don't chase representation-only differences;
  never override a miss a unit test deliberately asserts.
- **Covered and clean.** Add or extend a case in
  `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, red-before-green; the full
  `npm test` must be green (postcondition: *suite*). Never weaken a test, lower the
  gate, or hand-edit a GENERATED file — commit the regenerated baseline + scorecard
  as produced.

If no clean generic win emerges, print `No generic generic-coverage improvement found.`
and stop (this is a fully valid, successful outcome — do NOT create a branch or PR).

## 4. Postcondition

Pass every value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan as arguments:

```sh
bash .claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/generic-extractor-improvements/postconditions.sh "<recovered value>" ...
```

- Exit 0 → the win is valid; go to step 5.
- **Non-zero → the run has FAILED.** Do not retry and do not open a PR; surface the
  failure so guiding prose can be re-introduced to this routine. Report this clearly
  as a FAILURE in your final report.

## 5. Open the PR (never merge)

regenerated GENERATED artifacts, and push with `git push -u origin claude/generic-coverage/2026-08-02`.

"What happens when Tel Aviv memories meet a young imagination?

Join us for a special intergenerational activity – a journey of stories, memories, and creativity through the story of Tel Aviv-Yafo.

At the center of it all are unique postcards that bring the city’s stories to life through our annual art exhibition.

We start with a guided tour of the museum, where participants come face to face with moments, places, and people from the city’s history.

253	  // strict: a language with official standing in countries whose zones can
254	  // differ (en, es, fr, de, it, nl, pt, ar, ru, zh, sv, da, tr, el, ro, …) is
255	  // NOT here — a locale hint must never be able to point at the wrong country.
256	  const LANG_COUNTRY = {
257	    he: "IL",
258	    ja: "JP",
259	    ko: "KR",
260	    th: "TH",
261	    vi: "VN",
262	    pl: "PL",
263	    hu: "HU",
264	    cs: "CZ",

275	    nb: "NO",
276	    nn: "NO",
277	    no: "NO",
278	  };

280	  // Normalize a page-stated country (alpha-2 code in any case, or a name) to a
281	  // COUNTRY_TIMEZONES key; "" when it isn't a country we can place.
282	  function countryCode(raw) {
283	    const s = typeof raw === "string" ? GCal.clean(raw) : "";
284	    if (!s) return "";
285	    const code = s.toUpperCase();
286	    if (COUNTRY_TIMEZONES[code]) return code;
287	    return COUNTRY_NAMES[s.toLowerCase()] || "";
288	  }
289	
290	  // The zone's UTC offset (in minutes) at `instant`, read off Intl so no tz data
291	  // of our own is needed; null when the zone can't be resolved.
292	  function zoneOffsetMinutes(tz, instant) {
293	    let parts;
294	    try {
295	      parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
296	        timeZone: tz,
297	        hourCycle: "h23",
298	        year: "numeric",
299	        month: "2-digit",
300	        day: "2-digit",
301	        hour: "2-digit",
302	        minute: "2-digit",
303	        second: "2-digit",
304	      }).formatToParts(new Date(instant));
305	    } catch (e) {
306	      return null;
307	    }
308	    const g = (type) => Number((parts.find((p) => p.type === type) || {}).value);
309	    const localAsUTC = Date.UTC(g("year"), g("month") - 1, g("day"), g("hour"), g("minute"), g("second"));
310	    return Math.round((localAsUTC - instant) / 60000);
311	  }
312	
313	  // Every explicit UTC offset among the extracted start/end values, paired with
314	  // its instant. "Z" and floating/date-only values contribute nothing (see
315	  // header); a zone must reproduce EVERY pair to count as matching.
316	  function offsetPairs(values) {
317	    const pairs = [];
318	    for (const v of values || []) {
319	      const m = /([+-])(\d{2}):?(\d{2})$/.exec(v || "");
320	      if (!m) continue;
321	      const instant = Date.parse(v);
322	      if (Number.isNaN(instant)) continue;
323	      pairs.push({ minutes: (m[1] === "-" ? -1 : 1) * (+m[2] * 60 + +m[3]), instant });
324	    }
325	    return pairs;
326	  }
327	
328	  function zoneMatchesOffsets(tz, pairs) {
329	    return pairs.every((p) => zoneOffsetMinutes(tz, p.instant) === p.minutes);
330	  }
331	
332	  // The single IANA zone the page's inline scripts state, or "" when they state
333	  // none — or several different ones (a cross-venue listing).
334	  function statedTimezone() {
335	    const found = new Set();
336	    const re = /\\?"time[zZ]one\\?"\s*:\s*\\?"([^"\\]{1,40})\\?"/g;
337	    const scripts = GCal.scriptsText();
338	    let m;
339	    while ((m = re.exec(scripts))) {
340	      if (GCal.isValidTimezone(m[1])) found.add(m[1]);
341	    }
342	    return found.size === 1 ? [...found][0] : "";
343	  }
344	
345	  // The venue country the page's own structured data states: JSON-LD address
346	  // first (unanimous across the events that name one — several different
347	  // countries mean a multi-country listing, which also blocks the page-level
348	  // meta fallbacks), else the og/business place metas or geo.region.
349	  function venueCountry() {
350	    const fromLd = new Set();
351	    for (const ld of GCal.embeddedEvents.find()) {
352	      let loc = ld.location;
353	      if (Array.isArray(loc)) loc = loc[0];
354	      const addr = loc && typeof loc === "object" ? loc.address : null;
355	      let country = addr && typeof addr === "object" ? addr.addressCountry : null;
356	      if (country && typeof country === "object") country = country.name;
357	      const code = countryCode(country);
358	      if (code) fromLd.add(code);
359	    }
360	    if (fromLd.size) return fromLd.size === 1 ? [...fromLd][0] : "";
361	    return (
362	      countryCode(GCal.meta("og:country-name") || GCal.meta("business:contact_data:country_name")) ||
363	      countryCode((GCal.meta("geo.region") || "").split("-")[0])
364	    );
365	  }
366	
367	  // Country-code TLDs whose ISO-3166 alpha-2 code differs from the TLD label.
368	  // ".uk" is the only one in everyday use (GB is the alpha-2); the rest of the
369	  // ccTLD space is its own alpha-2, so a plain uppercase of the label is right.
370	  const CCTLD_COUNTRY = { UK: "GB" };
371	
372	  // The page's own locale country — "" unless every locale signal agrees. An
373	  // explicit region subtag ("he-IL", "en_US") wins over the language; a bare
374	  // language resolves only through the strict LANG_COUNTRY list; and when
375	  // NEITHER named a country, the host's own country-code TLD stands in.
376	  function localeCountry() {
377	    const found = new Set();
378	    const langAttr = document.documentElement ? document.documentElement.getAttribute("lang") : "";
379	    for (const raw of [langAttr, GCal.meta("og:locale")]) {
380	      const m = /^([a-z]{2,3})(?:[-_]([a-z]{2}))?\b/i.exec(GCal.clean(raw));
381	      if (!m) continue;
382	      const region = (m[2] || "").toUpperCase();
383	      if (region) {
384	        if (COUNTRY_TIMEZONES[region]) found.add(region);
385	        continue;
386	      }
387	      const byLang = LANG_COUNTRY[m[1].toLowerCase()];
388	      if (byLang) found.add(byLang);
389	    }
390	    if (found.size) return found.size === 1 ? [...found][0] : "";
391	    return hostCountry();
392	  }
393	
394	  // The country whose registry the page is published under, read off the host's
395	  // country-code TLD (".co.il"/".gov.il" -> IL, ".fr" -> FR, ".co.uk" -> GB);
396	  // "" for a generic TLD (.com/.org/.social) or a code we can't place.
397	  //
398	  // Deliberately a LOCALE-kind hint, never a country one: a ccTLD describes the
399	  // SITE, exactly like <html lang> — a Tel Aviv cinema's .co.il says nothing
400	  // about where any particular screening happens — so it can only corroborate a
401	  // venue country the page itself stated, never name one. That bound is what
402	  // makes a ccTLD in vanity use (".co", ".io", ".fm") harmless here: the country
403	  // is always the page's own address, and the hint can only agree or disagree
404	  // with it. It is also the WEAKEST locale signal, consulted only when <html
405	  // lang>/og:locale named no country, so a vanity ccTLD can never contradict a
406	  // locale the page actually declared.
407	  function hostCountry() {
408	    const tld = (location.hostname.split(".").pop() || "").toUpperCase();
409	    if (!/^[A-Z]{2}$/.test(tld)) return "";
410	    const code = CCTLD_COUNTRY[tld] || tld;
411	    return COUNTRY_TIMEZONES[code] ? code : "";
412	  }
413	
414	  // Decide the page's ctz. `values` are the extracted events' start/end strings
415	  // (they carry any UTC offset the page declared for the event itself). See the
416	  // header for the accepted hint combinations; anything less corroborated is "".
417	  function deriveCtz(values) {
418	    const pairs = offsetPairs(values);
419	    const stated = statedTimezone();
420	    if (stated) {
421	      // A stated zone still needs one independent agreeing hint — some
422	      // platforms embed the VIEWER's timezone, not the venue's.
423	      if (pairs.length) return zoneMatchesOffsets(stated, pairs) ? stated : "";
424	      const country = venueCountry();
425	      return country && COUNTRY_TIMEZONES[country].includes(stated) ? stated : "";
426	    }
427	    const country = venueCountry();
428	    if (!country) return "";
429	    const zones = COUNTRY_TIMEZONES[country];
430	    if (pairs.length) {
431	      const matching = zones.filter((z) => zoneMatchesOffsets(z, pairs));
432	      return matching.length === 1 ? matching[0] : "";
433	    }
434	    return zones.length === 1 && localeCountry() === country ? zones[0] : "";
435	  }
436	
437	  return { deriveCtz, COUNTRY_TIMEZONES };
438	})());

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Postconditions for the weekly generic-coverage routine
# (.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/generic-extractor-improvements/task.md).
#
# Runs AFTER the agent has made a candidate change, and bundles every
# deterministic validation that a "win" is clean, generic, real and non-regressing.
#   Exit 0   → the win is valid; finalize and open the PR.
#   Non-zero → a postcondition FAILED. Mark the run failed; do NOT retry and do
#              NOT open a PR. A failure means this deliberately-lean spec let the
#              agent produce an invalid change — the fix is to re-introduce guiding
#              prose to the routine, not to loop.
#
# Pass every value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan as arguments,
# so the jsdom-artifact trap can be checked automatically:
#   postconditions.sh "<recovered value 1>" "<recovered value 2>" ...
#
# Checks (all deterministic):
#   1. SCOPE — the diff touches ONLY the core generic extractor and its allowed
#      companions: generic-extractor.js and the shared helpers/*.js (the generic
#      extractor), a covering test in extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js,
#      and the regenerated generic-coverage GENERATED artifacts. A custom/<site>.js
#      edit or a host special-case is out of scope — it isn't a GENERIC win. (This
#      enforces WHICH files changed; whether the rule keys off a widely-used
#      convention rather than one page's quirk is the agent's judgment.)
#   2. SUITE — `npm test` is green. Runs the whole offline+live+UI suite, including
#      the generic-coverage high-watermark gate, which FAILS on any field
#      regression. (Red-before-green and authoring the covering test are the
#      agent's job; this asserts the end state.)
#   3. WIN — the regenerated baseline really improved on the committed (pre-change)
#      baseline: every headline % is >= the committed value and at least one is
#      strictly greater. A change that improves nothing, or lifts one field while
#      dropping another, is not a clean win. (Compares the working tree to the base
#      ref, so no state has to be carried over from preconditions.)
#   4. JSDOM — no value passed as an argument is a jsdom-only artifact. The offline
#      body-text scan reads document.body.textContent, which INCLUDES <script> JSON
#      (Next.js __NEXT_DATA__), <noscript>, <style>, <select>/<option> — none of
#      which Chrome's innerText exposes, so a win matching only such content is
#      illusory; a real win comes from visible text or a Chrome-read DOM attribute
#      (meta / JSON-LD / microdata / <time datetime>). (grep can't see CSS-hidden
#      text — eyeball that separately. And widening a body-text scan-window cap can
#      make a DIFFERENT case start matching a <script> blob it never reached: before
#      raising any cap, re-run the whole corpus at the new size — ideally with
#      <script>/<style>/<noscript> stripped first, approximating innerText — and
#      confirm no other case gains a wrong value; pick a bound comfortably above the
#      real win but below the nearest offending blob.)

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(git -C "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

fail() { echo "POSTCONDITION FAILED — mark this run failed, do not retry: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

ref=origin/main
git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ref=main
git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ref=HEAD

# ── 1. SCOPE ──
allowed='^(extension/event-extractors/generic-extractor\.js|extension/event-extractors/helpers/[^/]+\.js|extension-test/event-extractors/extraction\.test\.js|dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage\.(baseline\.GENERATED\.json|GENERATED\.md))$'
changed="$( { git diff --name-only "$ref"...HEAD 2>/dev/null; git diff --name-only HEAD 2>/dev/null; \
              git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | sed '/^$/d' )"
offenders="$(printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep -Ev "$allowed" || true)"
[ -z "$offenders" ] || fail "out-of-scope changes (only the generic extractor may change):
$(printf '  %s\n' $offenders)"

# ── 2. SUITE ──
npm test || fail "npm test is not green"

# ── 3. WIN ──
blpath="dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json"
pre_json="$(git show "$ref:$blpath" 2>/dev/null)" || fail "no committed baseline at $ref to compare against"
post_json="$(cat "$blpath" 2>/dev/null)" || fail "regenerated baseline missing — run the live suite first"
node -e '
  const pre = JSON.parse(process.argv[1]);
  const post = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);
  const fields = ["criticalFieldsPct", "allFieldsPct"];
  const regressed = fields.filter(f => post[f] < pre[f]);
  const improved  = fields.filter(f => post[f] > pre[f]);
  const show = fields.map(f => `${f} ${pre[f]}→${post[f]}`).join(", ");
  if (regressed.length) { console.error(`regressed: ${regressed.join(", ")} (${show})`); process.exit(1); }
  if (!improved.length) { console.error(`no improvement over baseline (${show})`); process.exit(1); }
  console.log(`win: ${show}`);
' "$pre_json" "$post_json" || fail "coverage did not cleanly improve over the committed baseline"

# ── 4. JSDOM ──
for value in "$@"; do
  [ -n "$value" ] || continue
  node -e '
    const fs = require("fs"), path = require("path");
    const value = process.argv[1];
    const dir = "dev/requirements/extractor/data/server-fetched";
    const strip = s => s.replace(/<(script|style|noscript)\b[^>]*>[\s\S]*?<\/\1>/gi, "");
    const hidden = [];
    for (const f of fs.readdirSync(dir).filter(n => n.endsWith(".html"))) {
      const html = fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, f), "utf8");
      if (!html.includes(value)) continue;
      if (!strip(html).includes(value)) hidden.push(f);
    }
    if (hidden.length) { console.error("only inside <script>/<style>/<noscript>: " + hidden.join(", ")); process.exit(1); }
  ' "$value" || fail "recovered value is a jsdom-only artifact (illusory in Chrome): \"$value\""
done

echo "All postconditions passed — the win is valid. Finalize and open the PR."
exit 0
postconditions.sh
task.md
task.mjs

Any "fix" here (including the real ISO bug below) would be an illusory win.

Only locale/ccTLD signals exist, which `helpers/derive-timezone.js` deliberately refuses to let mint a zone on their own. Any gain requires weakening the #674/#676 refusal contract — explicitly forbidden.
- **`eventLengthInMinutes` (0/11).** No page in the corpus publishes schema.org `duration` on a case that grades it (checked eventbrite ×2, telavivcinematheque ×4, edfringe ×5 — all get it from site-specific inline JSON). The one page that does publish `"duration":"PT2H"` (somo) has it left EMPTY by its dedicated source, so filling it generically would be ungraded and would break strict live-case parity.
- **`description` (19 `~` + 7 `✗`).** Every near-miss is site-shaped, not convention-shaped: meetup ×3 / eventer / eventim / eventbrite-games-for-change publish a **site-truncated** description in both JSON-LD and `og:description` (the full text lives in the site's own Apollo/Next state); secrettelaviv/thinkdrink/telavivcinematheque ×4 need the article body; somo's JSON-LD is Markdown whose stripped form still differs (bullet prefixes, paragraph spacing). The one genuinely close case (`eventbrite-1989775742810`) differs solely by `normalizeBlock` collapsing a double space — I prototyped "don't HTML-normalize a tag-free JSON-LD description" and rejected it: it makes the common templated-indentation case strictly worse, so it isn't an improvement, just a score nudge.
- **`location` (4 `~` + 8 `✗`).** `barby` needs a hardcoded venue name absent from every meta tag (only `apple-mobile-web-app-title`/document title carry it); `luma` and `somo` need DOM text the JSON-LD `Place` doesn't hold (I confirmed dropping the hierarchy-breaking `addressRegion`-after-country from `flattenLocation` still wouldn't match); `tel-aviv` names a different (more specific) venue than the page's structured address; `comy`/`seatgeek`/`tabitisrael` need site-specific enumeration.
- **Untapped structural conventions.** Swept all 36 fixtures for `itemprop`, `<time datetime>`, `event:start_time`, and hCalendar (`vevent`/`dtstart`): every present signal is already consumed by `generic-extractor.js`, and no fixture carries microformats or an unread microdata property.

Ran `gcec/generic-extractor-improvements` (slot `w2026-08-02`). Result: **no clean generic win found** — this is the expected, successful common case; no branch or PR was opened, no files were left changed, working tree clean.

Baseline (unchanged): `criticalFieldsPct 76.9%` (83/108), `allFieldsPct 57.9%` (121/209), 36 shared cases, gate ✓. Full `npm run test:live` green (59 pass, 1 skip).

Candidates investigated and ruled out:
- **edfringe cluster** (biggest mass: 5 `~` starts + 20 `✗` fields) — confirmed via experiment to be a jsdom-only artifact (`document.body.textContent` sees Next.js `__NEXT_DATA__` JSON that Chrome's `innerText` never exposes); any fix here would be an illusory win. In passing, found a real (but separately-actionable) bug: `parseDateFromText`'s ISO regex at `extension/event-extractors/helpers/dates.js:64` doesn't allow fractional seconds, silently dropping a trailing `Z` and reinterpreting a UTC instant as floating local time. Not filed as a coverage win since fixing it would only move the jsdom-illusory edfringe cases; worth a human follow-up as a standalone bugfix.
- **`ctz`** (19 misses) — no missing case declares a venue country/IANA zone via any page signal; filling it would require weakening the `derive-timezone.js` two-independent-hints refusal contract (#674/#676), which is forbidden.
- **`eventLengthInMinutes`** (0/11) — no graded case publishes a usable `duration`; the one page that does (`somo`) is deliberately left empty by its dedicated source, so filling it generically would break strict parity.
- **`description`** (19 `~` + 7 `✗`) — every near-miss is site-shaped (truncated JSON-LD/OG vs. full site state, or needing article body), not convention-shaped; the one close case only differs by whitespace normalization and a fix there regresses the common templated case.
- **`location`** (4 `~` + 8 `✗`) — each miss needs page-specific enumeration or DOM text not present in any structured signal.
- Swept all 36 fixtures for `itemprop`, `<time datetime>`, `event:start_time`, hCalendar — no unread structural signal found.

No GitHub objects other than this issue were touched (tracker issue #366 not touched — nothing to log there for a no-win run).

Converging: closing as completed within the `open-pr` outcome ceiling (no PR opened, which is within bounds).
